comparison: Perfect agreement on SIRT1/SIRT3 induction claims (C36-C43). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly acknowledges the induction findings and notes the re-analysis makes results more convincing.

Perfect agreement on SPI-1/SPI-2 dependency claims (C44-C47). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer acknowledges Salmonella's ability to modulate sirtuins through virulence factors without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on M2 polarization and bacterial proliferation claims (C48-C50). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly states macrophages were skewed toward M2 phenotype allowing bacterial hyper-proliferation.

Perfect agreement on bacterial survival reduction upon SIRT1/3 knockdown/inhibition claims (C51-C52). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge the knockdown experiments and describe the study as well-designed.

Perfect agreement on cytokine modulation claims (C53-C54, C56). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer implicitly accepts the cytokine data when acknowledging increased inflammation findings.

Perfect agreement on M1-to-M2 shift during infection claims (C57-C59). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly states macrophages were skewed toward M2 phenotype and editor notes valuable contribution to understanding pathogen-host interactions.

Perfect agreement on ROS production and NAC rescue claims (C60, C68-C70). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly accepts that effects are due to increased ROS production by macrophages.

Perfect agreement on histological inflammation findings (C61-C62). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer accepts increased inflammation in inhibitor-treated mice, with histological data consistent with accepted cytokine and ROS findings.

Disagreement on SIRT1-p65 interaction mechanism claims (C63-C67). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches. Peer reviewer rates UNCERTAIN, noting the link is weak and experimental evidence is lacking to prove proposed mechanisms, describing data as correlative.

Disagreement on metabolic shift claims (C71-C79). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches across in vitro and in vivo models. Peer reviewer rates UNCERTAIN, stating authors try to establish a weak link with metabolism, experimental evidence is lacking, and criticizing low data quality and too many pathways being investigated.

Perfect agreement on SPI-2 requirement for metabolic shift (C80). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer acknowledges the pathogen interaction mechanisms and raises no specific concerns about this finding.

Disagreement on bacterial metabolic profile claims (C81-C85). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with data from both in vitro and in vivo models. Peer reviewer rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the finding but stating experimental evidence is lacking to prove mechanisms and criticizing the weak metabolic link.

Disagreement on SIRT1-HIF1α mechanism claims (C86-C87, C89). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with co-IP and functional validation. Peer reviewer rates UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating the HIF1α acetylation data is correlative and needs further experiments to prove the mechanism.

Disagreement on SIRT3-PDHA1 mechanism claims (C90-C91). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with co-IP demonstrating interaction and acetylation changes. Peer reviewer rates UNCERTAIN, stating experimental evidence is lacking to prove proposed mechanisms and data is correlative.

Perfect agreement on in vivo susceptibility claims (C92-C97). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly accepts the dissemination findings despite noting they are counterintuitive, and acknowledges the revised manuscript makes results more complete and convincing. OpenEval also addresses C98 (Cybb-/- mice) which peer reviewer includes in same result.

Partial overlap on in vivo findings. OpenEval R16 addresses NADPH oxidase mechanism (C98) finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R14 covers broader in vivo susceptibility claims (C92-C98) also rating SUPPORTED. Both accept the in vivo data despite paradoxical nature.

Perfect agreement on in vivo inflammatory mediators (C99-C102). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer accepts that effects are due to increased inflammation and ROS production in vivo without raising specific concerns.

Perfect agreement on cell-type-specific effects in spleen (C103-C107). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly acknowledges reduced bacterial burden in macrophages despite increased dissemination, and notes revised flow cytometry analysis makes results more convincing.

Partial overlap on in vivo ROS and inflammation. OpenEval R19 addresses ROS in tissue homogenates (C108) finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R17 covers both ROS and histological inflammation (C108-C109) also rating SUPPORTED. Both accept the in vivo oxidative stress findings.

Partial overlap on liver pathology. OpenEval R20 addresses histological liver pathology (C109) finding it SUPPORTED. Peer R17 covers both ROS and histological findings (C108-C109) also rating SUPPORTED. Both accept the histopathological evidence of inflammation.

Perfect agreement on AAV knockdown validation (C110-C111). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer states revised manuscript addressed all comments and results are now more complete and convincing with genetic validation.

Agreement on uncertainty of novelty claim (C112). Both evaluations rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the claim cannot be fully evaluated without comprehensive literature review. Peer reviewer acknowledges potential value but notes experimental evidence is lacking to prove mechanisms, particularly the weak metabolic link.
